name: 2100 S. Prairie Avenue — the alley building of the house at 2100 (district draft; refined by T-1937)

grade.why: Known from maps or written records; no picture of it has been found.

documented_range.note: The draft claims the 1904 target and no more: the 1911 sheet draws the building and the T-1842 census rules it present in 1904 (present_as_mapped). Its building and loss dates are the per-building ticket's to read.

placement.position_note: The rear corner of the main body's rectangle (lot frame u 1.750, v -9.500 m from the middle of the rear lot line), through the T-1250 fit of the sheet: the sheet's georeference carries no independent check: its own fit residual is 0.05 m RMS on its control crossings, a similarity on two degrees of freedom that says little away from them, plus about a pixel (0.19 m) of trace on this coarser copy. Rotation -0.614 degrees turns the plan's u axis onto the lot's own rear-to-street line.
placement.symbolic_location: 2100 S. Prairie Avenue, parcel prairie_2100 (data/street_grid/1904.json), west side of Prairie Avenue, Prairie Avenue, 20th to 22nd Street (Sanborn 1911 vol. 3 sheet 35).

footprint.note: The main body: the largest rectangle that fits inside the traced main part (u toward the street, v along the front). The building's other rectangles are in draft_plan.

stories.note: The census reading '2-storey brick building on the alley lettered PRIVATE WAGON HOUSE, its south part marked as a stable': 2 storeys.

construction.note: The trace's fabric colour on the main part: brick.

draft_plan.note: Rectangles fitted inside the traced parts by the rules' fit (cell 0.25 m, at most 3 a part, to 90% cover): s35fp-2100-b2 outline (main, brick), rectangle 1 of that part; the part's rectangles cover 77% of its fill; s35fp-2100-b2 outline (main, brick), rectangle 2 of that part; the part's rectangles cover 77% of its fill; s35fp-2100-b2 outline (main, brick), rectangle 3 of that part; the part's rectangles cover 77% of its fill. Roles: the main part's largest rectangle is the main body; a shallow rectangle at the front is a bay; the sheet's ranges, porches and stone fronts keep their roles. Storeys per piece and roof per piece are the draft rules' (reconstructed).

draft_elevation.note: RECONSTRUCTED by the draft rules, family row 'service' overlaid with the frontage row: The John B. Sherman house (Burnham & Root, 1874), standing empty in 1904 after Sherman's death: the register's 'steep slate roof and stone dormers' and 'carved chimney tops' as a steep hip with dormers and three stacks over the 3S.B. brick body, the curved stair and clustered columns as a central entrance. The 1911 lettering McCORMICK MEDICAL COLLEGE is a later use and is not drawn; the oriel on its column is T-1919's. Heights are the rules' starting values inside RECONSTRUCTION-RULES.md's ranges; bays, entrance side, chimneys and dormers are counts the family rules choose, and the seed 1165633831 only tints the fabric inside +-6 %. Liberty L-draft-prairie-20-22-west-2351.

draft.note: The draft's own provenance: the pass that wrote it, the rows it read and the tickets that replace it attribute by attribute under this id.

function.note: The 1911 sheet reads '2-storey brick building on the alley lettered PRIVATE WAGON HOUSE, its south part marked as a stable'. The Sherman stable and wagon house; a private wagon house in 1911, so no 1904 backcast of use is needed.

citations.citation: Sanborn Map Company. Insurance Maps of Chicago, Illinois, Volume 3. New York: Sanborn Map Company, 1911. Sheet 35.

what_it_does_not_supply: Anything as of 1904 on its own authority. It is a 1911 survey; Glessner House's reading that everything on sheets 20, 28 and 35 but 1609-1611 and 1620 Prairie stood in 1904 is attributed guidance, recorded in that README, and not checked by this record
A construction date for any building it draws
Elevations, grades, curb heights or fill depths -- no Sanborn sheet carries a level
Architecture above the footprint beyond its story count, material colour and roof symbol
Any lake edge: the sheet ends at Calumet Avenue
